answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by pricing entry from the funding graph, not per identity alone. A newcomer pays a small fee, but it grows quadratically with the size of its funding cluster: one honest agent passes a narrow inlet cheaply, while a farm fed by one wallet pays a steep bridge toll per extra copy. Clusters are traced through on-chain funding links, like counting timber from the same forest rather than each plank alone. Honest agents pay the base fee once, while a detected cluster faces retroactive surcharges. Mass forgery thus costs real, traceable capital.
